summary: Mark A. Nathan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. His career includes positions as Coordinator at UCLA, Visiting Professor at Kangwon National University, and Lecturer at University at Buffalo.

Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He worked at SOAS and held appointments as department chair and Associate Professor at the University of Sydney.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar in sinology and philosophy. He served as an Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1994 to 2004, before becoming Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2004.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and the University of Exeter. After lecturing at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995), he served as Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University from 1995 to 2025.

Mark Elliott is a historian working in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as professor of history at UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University around 2003.

Mark Jan Dresden was a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Amsterdam and Utrecht under Jan Gonda, as well as with Harold Walter Bailey and Walter Bruno Henning, before teaching at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and Indology. After earning degrees from the University of Illinois, Columbia, and UC Berkeley, he served as a professor and Director of Global and International Studies at UC Santa Barbara and at Claremont McKenna College.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held faculty posts at the State University of New York, University at Albany, SUNY, and served as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair in Japanese Studies at UC Berkeley.

Mark Liberman is a scholar in linguistics and computational linguistics. Educated at Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, he held an academic post at the University of Pennsylvania's Department of Linguistics from around 1990.
Mark Owen is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Rowe is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He holds a post at McMaster University, where he is attested as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and completed his DPhil at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson.

Mark Siderits is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught at Illinois State University from circa 1979 to 2007, later becoming Emeritus Professor of Philosophy there, and served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (2007–2012).

Mark Singleton is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. A former pupil of Elizabeth De Michelis, he earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge and served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London.

Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD in 1978 from the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served as a Professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Mark Teeuwen is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who earned his MA and PhD from Leiden University. After lecturing at Cardiff University (1994–1999), he was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Mark Unno is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University, subsequently holding posts at Brown University (~1994–1998) and the University of Oregon (~1998).

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He has held positions at the University of Bonn, UC Berkeley, The New School, and served as Global Senior Advisor at the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy in 2024.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD in 2012 at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, working as a project researcher at Heidelberg University and on the faculty at Vienna.

Marsha Weidner specializes in sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at UC Berkeley, she served as assistant professor of art history at the University of Virginia and Professor of the History of Art at the University of Kansas.
